limits.llmPick: Demand facets and rivals are picked by the LLM — modifiers from the related queries are split with a brand dictionary, and of what remains only occasion, use and feature are kept. The picks are in work/curate.json.
limits.noCombo: Some categories have no combined query, so the naming axis could not be measured. The attach rate - on those rows is not 0% but missing volume data, and the journey axis decides the verdict.
limits.noEvidence: {n} of these have zero evidence in either the branded related queries or the branded journeys — they were specified by a person or came in another way.
limits.oneSeed: A demand facet is judged from the journeys starting at one facet query. Someone searching the same situation in different words is not included.
limits.scope: Only {done} of {total} candidates were studied. A category we did not study was not judged to be without opportunity — it simply was not looked at in this run —
limits.thin: {n} categories were left out of the demand-facet deep dive. Too few facet candidates come out of the related queries (fewer than 30 modifiers), so a deep dive would return an empty table —
limits.thinTail: . This does not mean there is no opportunity — it means this axis cannot measure it.
map.note: Cells = 12-month volume of related queries containing that brand name · colour = 1st/2nd in that category · click a row to open per-brand share and related queries
method.alias: Alias rule — product and line names fold into the parent brand, and common misspellings fold in too.
method.facetAxis: A demand facet is judged by how many branded queries appear across the {npaths} search journeys from that facet query — searches that attach a brand name to the facet barely exist, so they are not used.
method.journeyAxis: The journey axis counts the distinct branded queries appearing anywhere across the {npaths} journeys from path_finder — the same number ListeningMind PathView shows when you filter the keyword list by brand name. “First at” is how many steps after the seed it first appears. A branded query repeated across journeys counts once. The verdict follows the 2x rule; under 3 on both sides it is “none”.
method.namingAxis: The naming axis is share of search — we keep only the related queries that contain a brand name (aliases included) and use the combined branded query volume of our brand plus rivals as the denominator (this differs from a QueryFinder topic total — generic queries are not in the denominator). Leading, Contested and Trailing follow the 2x rule between our brand and the leader. Unclaimed means the branded share of category demand (branded query volume ÷ (that volume + the category term's volume)) is under 10%, or branded query volume is under 1,000 a year — a position people search without naming a brand.
orbit.howto: Drag a circle to move it, drag the background to pan. The mouse wheel zooms while over the graph.
orbit.logScale: log scale (one category is so large the rest would be indistinguishable, so the size gap is compressed)
orbit.noCircle: Categories with no branded queries, so no circle was drawn:
orbit.note: Circle size = that category's all-brand volume (ours + rivals' branded queries, 12 months) · fill height = {own}'s share of it · figures = {own} volume / all-brand volume
orbit.title: {own} share of search by category
priority.adjacentForm: An adjacent market in another form
priority.lead: The map's positions are regrouped against what {own} actually sells on its official store. The same “Trailing” is a weakness to fix if there is a product, and not a weakness but a missing product if there is none. Selling status follows the official store's category and product listings; anything we could not verify is placed under “no product here”.
report.lede: Starting from one brand name ({own}), we found the product categories this brand spans and looked at who owns the name in each and where the search journey goes. Below each category sits one more level: demand facets (occasion, use, feature, form, grade).

report.title: Brand Competition · Category Map

s4.axisLead: The more branded queries inside the related queries, the more the naming axis fills in; the fewer, the more it leans on the journey.
s4.crossLead: The name sticks but the search goes elsewhere afterwards, or the reverse. This value is not used in the verdict badge.
s4.groupLead: A pattern the category rows cannot show.

s4.keepTakeLeadNone: Defend {keep}. Nothing to take — no category at or above the median ({med}) trails by 2x or more.
s4.keepTakeTitle: Where to defend and where to take
s4.lead: Only what a single row cannot show — sections with no value are omitted.
s4.mismatchLead: One category row cannot show this. It asks whether a category you are defending already has facets you are losing.
s4.mismatchNone: No disagreement — the category verdict holds at the demand-facet level too.
s4.mismatchTitle: Where the category verdict and its demand facets disagree
s4.missFacet: {n} deep-dive categories whose demand facets could not be measured —
s4.missOwn: {n} categories whose related queries contain no {own} query at all —
s4.rivalsLead: If they cluster on one rival, watch that brand; if they scatter, each position is a different fight.
s4.unmeasuredLead: What is listed here is not “there is none” but “this run cannot tell”.
s4.watchLead: Where the brands you specified appear. Measured across every category, separately from automatic discovery.
